rows.why: The rows that test the question are '2d' and '1d0h0m0s0ms', which need the d (day) unit along with h, m, s and ms. The pick supports d, h, m, s and ms. Item 9 (zero durations) only touches the '0s' row.
Item 5 asks whether whitespace is allowed. The scenario expects leading and trailing whitespace to be ignored, so '  45m\n' gives 2700000. The pick rejects any whitespace, including ' 1h'.

Several items cover parts of this table: item 1 covers '90', item 5 covers '3S' and '3 s', item 7 covers the empty string. Item 6 is closest, covering '1.5h', '-3s' and '+3s'. Its pick rejects decimals and signs, which matches. The '05s' and '３s' rows are not addressed by any item.
No item asks whether a count may exceed the next unit up, like '90m'. Item 11 covers how format spells such values, not whether parse accepts them.

Most rows ('30m1h', '5ms1s', '1s500ms2s') test descending unit order, which is item 3. The scenario rejects out-of-order units, but the pick accepts any order. Item 2 (repeated units) covers only '1h1h', and its pick agrees.
Item 8 asks about the upper limit. The pick rejects only totals above 9007199254740991, so exactly that value parses, as the scenario expects.
The pick rejects totals above 9007199254740991 ms with a ValueError, which matches rejecting '...992ms' and the huge ms count.

Most rows settle which spelling format picks. The scenario expects the largest-unit-first form (90000 gives '1m30s', 5400000 gives '1h30m'). The pick chooses the shortest string ('90s', '90m'). The 0 row is item 10, whose pick '0s' also disagrees with '0ms'.

The expected string depends on the spelling rule. The shortest-string pick would give '104249991d539m991ms' (19 characters) instead of '104249991d8h59m991ms' (20 characters). Item 12's limit only settles that the max value doesn't raise, and its pick allows it.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing gives the original number back.

Item 12 asks what format does with bool, float, negative and too-large values. The pick raises ValueError for all of them, matching -1, 9007199254740992, True and 1.0. The pick doesn't say what the message says, so the 'milliseconds' wording isn't confirmed.
